newsitem.title: CANADA: Minister hopes for CAI vote in days.
newsitem.headline: Minister hopes for CAI vote in days.

text.p: Canadian Labor Minister Alfonso Gagliano said on Wednesday he hoped members of the Canadian Auto Workers union would vote in "a matter of days" on a tough restructuring plan to save troubled Canadian Airlines Corp.
"I hope it's a matter of days," Gagliano told reporters shortly after saying he was using his power to order CAW members to vote on the company's restructuring scheme.
"I think we'll have to wait a day or two to know when the vote will be taken," Gagliano said.
He said he called Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove five minutes before issuing the directive, to ask whether he would change his mind and agree to hold a vote.
"He said his position was final," he said. "So I said, 'Well, you take your responsibility and I'll take mine.'"
The directive to the labor board was made about only two hours after a fruitless meeting among Hargrove, Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson and Canadian Airlines chief executive Kevin Benson.
"I think I gave a chance for the negotiating process to work. Unfortunately we are at an impasse," Gagliano said in explaining what he said was a rare decision to force a vote.
"It was definitely a very extraordinary measure. It's not an easy day for the minister of labor, but I have to take my responsibility."
He said the labor board was asking Canadian for the exact proposal "so that the members can have the proposal before them."
Anderson told reporters that Canadian had been damaged for the past five weeks.
"Five weeks is a very long time to bleed the way Canadian has bled. We want to make sure that company gets back on the road," he said.

Told by a reporter that Hargrove expressed surprise with the government move, Anderson responded: "Mr. Hargrove must have been asleep for much of the last five weeks if he did not expect us to take action, when he with his personal actions is preventing five unions, two companies and three governments from proceeding with the restructuring program."
Anderson added that five of the six unions were voting on Thursday.
